events.description:
REGISTER NOW
|
FREE IN-PERSON EVENT @ HMC |
Open to Sheridan Students.
C-Wing, 5th Floor.
Registration is required for entry.
FREE Lunch + Giveaways.
Make Your Student Voice Count 📢
Don’t miss the chance to vote on important bylaw changes that impact your Sheridan Life! Enjoy a FREE lunch and  giveaways while you share valuable feedback on the issues that matter most to you and your peers.
October 15th
Our
Annual General Meeting (AGM)
is a chance for you to learn about Sheridan Student Union’s impact from the 2025-2026 year. This year, we will also reveal our new mission, vision, and guiding principles. Be the first to see our organization’s renewed direction and the values that will guide our work moving forward.
Here’s What You Should Know About the Annual General Meeting (HMC)
The AGM will be held in-person at the HMC Campus (5th Floor) on October 15th, 2026.
OneCard is required for entry and all Sheridan students have the right to vote at the AGM
.
Register before October 8th, 2026 for access to the FREE Lunch!
Don’t miss the chance to share your feedback and
view SSU’s impact report from our last academic year
!
Attendees will have
a chance to win one of three $50 Walmart gift cards in our raffle.
Come for the governance, stay for the community, and maybe even leave with a prize!
If you cannot attend the AGM, but would like to have your vote count,
you will need to appoint someone as your “proxy” and complete the proxy section of the registration form.
Any member wishing to propose amendments or revisions to SSU Bylaw may submit a request through the process outlined in Section 11.3 of the SSU Bylaw.  A Bylaw Proposal Form can be requested from the Chief Returning Officer by email at:
ssui.cro@sheridancollege.ca
.
LEARN ABOUT OUR KEYNOTE SPEAKER
After last year’s success, we have the talented Jared Big Canoe returning to our AGM as a keynote speaker! He is Anishinaabe from the Chippewas of Georgina Island and a dedicated community leader. Jared holds deep knowledge of Indigenous protocols and a strong commitment to youth; he creates space for learning, growth, and celebration. Jared Big Canoe is both a Healer and an entrepreneur.

events.description:
REGISTER NOW
|
FREE EVENT | 18+ | Open to Sheridan Students ONLY
Bring your project or just bring your perspective 🗣️
Showcase your work, share your ideas, and explore Autism & ADHD Awareness. Bring a project you’ve created for a chance to win up to $500. 💰 Build for Change is a 2-hour, drop-in student showcase focused on Autism & ADHD Awareness. 🖌️
October 16th
Bring a project, artwork, research, app, video, or any other work you’ve created and share what it means to you. Projects can be creative, technical, analytical, or anything in between. Don’t have a project? You’re still welcome to drop in, explore the showcase, share your ideas, or create something at the event. 🎨📢
Here’s What You Should Know About Build for Change: EDI Student Project Showcase
This event will take place on Friday, October 16th, in The Den Quiet Area, Davis Campus, from 4:00 P.M. to 6:00 P.M.
Open to Sheridan Students ONLY
Sheridan students must bring their OneCard
Click Here for Additional Eligibility and Contest Rules
Sheridan Student Union is committed to providing accommodations for our events to everyone. If you require any additional support, please feel free to contact
navrosesingh.johal@sheridancollege.ca
Please specify the [Event Name] you have questions about in your email subject line
.
How Can You Participate?
Bring a project.
Submit or present something you've prepared, on your own or with a group. Winning projects earn prizes, are showcased in person and/or virtually, and are featured on the SSU website.
You could also come without a project and prepare on spot.
No preparation needed. Visit our interactive participation station and respond anonymously to prompts tied to the theme “Autism and ADHD Awareness”. How would you improve accessibility and inclusion on campus? What's an experience you've had related to the theme? What's one change Sheridan could make to better support students? Responses are displayed where appropriate so everyone can read and react to each other's ideas. Participants receive giveaways (while supplies last).
